sections.name: Point, NetworkSource, Facility, Terminal, ActivityRef
sections.title: Basic data shapes
sections.what: Defines the shapes of a map point, a data source, a facility, a terminal and an activity reference.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared description of the basic building blocks.

sections.name: Circuit, PICoverage, StationAsset, StationView
sections.title: Circuit and station shapes
sections.what: Defines circuits, the coverage of each project element, station assets, and the station view that holds them.
sections.why: Likely reason: groups the detailed station data into one structure.
sections.watch_out: Several fields are optional, so code reading them must handle missing values.

sections.name: ProgrammeNetwork, activityKey
sections.title: Programme shape and activity key
sections.what: Defines the full programme shape and a helper that makes one text key for each activity.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single key lets activities from different projects be compared and stored.
sections.watch_out: The key joins ids with a slash, so an id that contains a slash could match a different activity.

sections.name: endpointFacility
sections.title: Finding a terminal's facility
sections.what: Finds the facility that a terminal belongs to, or returns nothing if either is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the view show which facility a terminal sits in.
sections.watch_out: A missing match returns nothing without an error, so callers must handle that case.

sections.name: localAssets
sections.title: Filtering station assets
sections.what: Keeps the assets that match the chosen configuration or are shared, and drops grounding assets unless underground is shown.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the view show one configuration at a time without grounding clutter.
sections.watch_out: The underground flag hides grounding assets, so turning it off removes them from every view.

summary: Defines the data shapes for the network view: facilities, terminals, circuits, station assets and the overall programme. It also has three small helpers for looking up and filtering that data.
purpose: Gives the network code one agreed description of its data, so mistakes are caught early.
why: Likely reason: typed shapes make the data's structure clear to every part of the code that uses it.
how: Declares the data shapes first, then builds a key helper for activities, a helper that finds a terminal's facility, and a helper that filters station assets by configuration and underground status.
inputs: Network data loaded from the backend, along with a configuration name and an underground flag for filtering.
outputs: Typed data shapes, a text key per activity, a facility or nothing, and a filtered asset list.
risks: The activity key joins project and activity ids with a slash, so ids that contain a slash could produce the same key. The helpers trust the data to be complete.
debug: If a lookup returns nothing, check that the terminal's facility id matches a facility id. If assets are missing from a view, check the configuration and underground settings passed in.
